comments.comment: This is so true, but it’s also so infuriating to have these shifting definitions. Thank you for addressing this!
They don't talk about the women who died from abortions
This was very informative and i definitely will be changing the way i talk about abortions because it is a large spectrum.

Mind you, if the women who want to get pregnant are dying from having miscarriages/not getting abortions and little girls are dying from getting pregnant due to being 🍇-ed, then all the people making children will possibly die out. Having an abortion is not easy, we ALL know that, but most of the time it's completely needed so a woman can try to give birth again later. Also abortion was created before medical industries started actually studying women's bodies properly instead of torturing them, so now that we are studying women's bodies and pregnancies we can start introducing abortions were the baby inside doesn't HAVE to be killed for the mother or little girl to be saved.

An abortion is the killing of a child. That has always been the definition of an abortion. Removing an ectopic pregnancy (an already dead child) is not an abortion. The abortion pills (plan b) and elective d&c are.

Abortion has a meaning and we all know it. Now I do think being clear is better generally but let’s not pretend it’s confusing even if the medical industry has for years tried to muddle things.
I've been saying this for so long! We need to have a clear definition on what they mean by "abortion". This sums it up perfectly to define elective vs medically necessary.
